title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Normal
text:
NORMAL traffic represents the dataset's benign class and should not be described as an incident without corroborating signals. Review packet and flow baselines, source and destination diversity, protocol mix, expected applications, and time-of-day seasonality. A Normal prediction does not prove a host is uncompromised. When a separate any-attack forecast is elevated, investigate the reason for the temporal risk without converting the current Normal label into an observed attack. Verify that the model feature schema and preprocessing match the actual inference stream. Suggested next steps: compare trends to historical baselines; sample suspicious sessions; check sensor health and missing features; review alerts from independent controls.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Analysis
text:
In UNSW-NB15, Analysis is a dataset attack-category label for activity associated with analysis and probing of services or weaknesses. It is not a specific MITRE technique or a verified root cause. Possible investigation clues include repeated service requests, unusual sequences of application requests, and broad targeting within a short interval. Corroborate with web/proxy, DNS, firewall and authentication logs where available. Check source and destination concentration, timestamps, application errors and whether similar traffic matches authorized vulnerability scanning. Suggested responses: validate the traffic against change calendars; investigate affected services; alert the service owner; consider narrowly scoped access restrictions if malicious traffic is confirmed. Avoid equating the label alone with exploitation.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Backdoor
text:
Backdoor is an UNSW-NB15 class describing traffic resembling covert or unauthorized access mechanisms. A flow classifier alone cannot establish persistence or identify malware. Useful corroboration may include unexpected remote access, unusual outbound destinations, periodic sessions, and account activity outside normal use. Examine endpoint process telemetry, firewall egress logs, authentication events and asset criticality. Suggested responses: prioritize affected hosts for investigation; verify remote access is authorized; preserve relevant logs; contain confirmed unauthorized access according to incident response policy; reset credentials only after scoping where appropriate. Be cautious: beaconing or persistence must not be asserted merely from the classification.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: DoS
text:
Denial of Service (DoS) aims to reduce availability by exhausting a network, service, or application resource. Indicators can include elevated packet or connection rates, bursty protocol concentration, repeated requests to the same endpoint and degradation reported by monitoring; the presence and direction of these indicators must be measured, not inferred from a model label. Investigate per-source and per-destination traffic, connection states, HTTP responses, firewall and load-balancer metrics, CPU and queue saturation, and baseline variability. Correlate with maintenance or legitimate traffic spikes. Defensive options when supported by evidence include traffic filtering, rate limiting, upstream DDoS mitigation, scaling, and incident escalation. Avoid applying aggressive blocks without checking legitimate impact. A general any-attack H10 forecast does not forecast a particular DoS attack.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Exploits
text:
Exploits is a broad UNSW-NB15 category, not a particular vulnerability identifier. Network features may reflect suspicious application or protocol interactions, but do not prove successful compromise. Investigate affected services, recent errors or crashes, authentication and web logs, and vulnerability exposure using inventory and asset context. Only link a CVE or MITRE technique when independent telemetry or a named software vulnerability supports it. Responses may include targeted log review, controlled patch or mitigation assessment, verified indicators of compromise, and escalation to the asset owner. Distinguish attempts from confirmed successful exploitation.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Fuzzers
text:
Fuzzers refers to dataset traffic associated with systematic varied or malformed input to software or protocols. Similar patterns can arise from authorized testing and benign QA. Possible investigation signals include many unusual payloads, malformed requests, repeated boundary-value inputs and high rates of error responses. Correlate with vulnerability-testing schedules, developer workflows, request logs and service stability metrics. Defensive steps include checking whether testing is approved, assessing affected endpoint resilience, reviewing error rates, and limiting clearly unauthorized probing if policy permits. Do not conclude an exploit succeeded based on a Fuzzers label alone.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Generic
text:
Generic is an UNSW-NB15 category, not the English word for all threats, and should not be automatically mapped to any one technique. Treat the class as a dataset-defined attack type whose exact semantics depend on the dataset's generation and labeling documentation. Investigate observable traffic characteristics such as unusual repetition, protocol fields, request concentration and deviations from local baseline. Correlate independent network alerts and session metadata before recommending containment. A Generic prediction cannot justify a claim about a particular intrusion method, credential attack or vulnerability without external evidence. Defensive response: validate features, inspect representative flows, preserve related evidence and escalate if independently suspicious.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Reconnaissance
text:
Reconnaissance in UNSW-NB15 denotes exploratory activity such as probing hosts, ports or services. Indicators may include one source contacting many destination ports, scanning across many hosts, or repeated connection attempts with few completed sessions, but those specifics require network flow evidence. Authorized inventory scans can look similar. Investigate source/destination diversity, destination port distribution, success/failure rates, scan authorization and time patterns. Check firewall and IDS logs. Defensive options include verifying authorization, reviewing exposed services, enabling appropriate rate controls or filtering, and investigating suspicious sources. Do not label a particular scanner or adversary based solely on the ML class.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Shellcode
text:
Shellcode is a dataset attack label associated with payloads intended to execute code. A network classification does not show that a payload ran successfully. Corroborate with network payload inspection when lawful and available, EDR process execution records, application crashes, memory alerts, IDS signatures and endpoint containment history. Determine exposure and service identity before making claims about exploitation. Follow approved incident procedures if credible execution indicators are found: preserve forensic artifacts, involve endpoint responders, and isolate confirmed affected systems when required. Avoid describing unverified malware execution or assigning a CVE without supporting evidence.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.

title: NetGuard UNSW-NB15 attack class: Worms
text:
Worms in UNSW-NB15 denotes traffic associated with self-propagating malware behavior. A single classified flow is not sufficient to establish network-wide infection or lateral movement. Corroborating signs may include similar suspicious traffic from multiple hosts, unexpected east-west connections, rapid expansion in reachable targets and endpoint detections. Investigate temporal propagation, host-to-host contacts, affected subnets, patch posture and EDR signals. Defensive actions when warranted can include isolating confirmed infected hosts, segmenting affected networks, blocking validated indicators, collecting forensic data and coordinating remediation. Preserve the distinction between class prediction and confirmed self-propagation.
This document is project-authored analyst guidance, not an official attribution or a direct mapping from UNSW-NB15 to MITRE ATT&CK. Use corroborating telemetry before any operational action.
